steps.why: TeruBot changes the cart and the saved list through this page: a "terucon:shop" event answered by tbApply* (state and persistence are the page's own), a queue in sessionStorage applied once the catalogue is loaded when the change was asked for on another page, and the room under TeruBot's button (--tb-bottom). Members of the page's component, kept in snippets/shop-terubot-members.txt (not a .js file: it only parses inside the class)
listen for TeruBot's "terucon:shop" events from the first render
once the saved cart is loaded, apply what TeruBot queued while another page was open (after the load, or the load would overwrite it)
keep TeruBot's button clear of the cart bar and the compare tray, with the same offsets the old Ask button used
a card from TeruBot links to /materials#<id> (a product, variant or finish id): open that product. Any other hash is routed as before

steps.why: PostHog analytics: page views, clicks and forms, and (studio page) the studio's own events, which its browser code sends to window.posthog but its server never gives a key for. The script asks GET /api/analytics, so no key is in the page

sign-in: the header link says Sign in or Account, and a request answered "please sign in" (the session ended) leads to the sign-in page. The script asks GET /api/auth/me, so nothing about the visitor is in the page

paste an address into a box marked data-import-urls and it asks "Import this photo?" (target C3). The script is a module served from /inspiration/assets/ (server/routes/inspiration.js), not inline text, so this page's runtime never rewrites it

the shop's "Find it from a photo" sheet has the same kind of input as the studio's "Take a photo" (a file input with capture=environment): on a phone it hands the screen to the camera app, the phone can throw this heavy page away meanwhile, and the photo never arrives. site/brand/studio-camera.js (shared with the studio) opens the camera inside the page instead and gives the sheet the picture as a chosen file; with no in-page camera it falls back to the camera app or the gallery. The address carries ?v=20261104 because /brand/* is cached for a day (app.js) and a phone that has used the studio holds the older script, which only knows the studio's input: change the number when this script changes
the shop's search box takes a pasted photo address (data-import-urls, see import-script)
the shop's own photo-match card is a frontend preview (TARGETS.md A1/C4); this points to the Finder, which actually searches the real catalogue (target C4)

the site chrome (site/brand/chrome.js) is the one header: the export's own header is not drawn once the chrome is on (the chrome's Saved and Cart buttons click its originals and mirror their counts); the menu overlay on a phone leads with the destinations; room for the bottom bar
insert:
<style>
/* the site chrome is the one header (site/brand/chrome.md); the export's own header stays in the page (the chrome's Saved and Cart buttons click its links and mirror their counts) but is not drawn while the chrome is on */
html.tc-chrome-on [data-nav] { display: none !important; }
/* menu overlay on a phone or small tablet: destinations lead */
[data-menu-dest] { display: none; }
@media (max-width: 819px) {
  [data-menu-dest] { display: flex; }
  [data-menu] > div { justify-content: flex-start !important; gap: 26px !important; padding: 12px 20px calc(28px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)) !important; }
  [data-menu-aside] > a { display: none !important; }
  [data-menu] nav a { font-size: 22px !important; padding: 13px 0 !important; }
}
/* the footer already has 96 px of room at its end; dock.css's own spacer would sit mid-page here (the body is only a frame) */
@media (max-width: 899px) {
  body::after { display: none !important; }
}
</style>
